inspiration: A handful of swimmers paddle miles up a guarded estuary by night to mine enemy shipping at its moorings, then try to walk home through a country that is now hunting them.
skeleton: a tiny infiltration element must work deep into a guarded DropShip mooring basin by stealth, place charges on hulls under repair where they cannot be defended by maneuver, and exfiltrate overland through a tightening search once the first explosion announces them, where the demolition is easy and the getting away is the mission
title: OPERATION SLACK TIDE
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} keeps its assault DropShips in the repair basin at {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}. The hulls sit in the graving docks with their drives torn apart for a rebuild, and {EMPLOYER} wants them destroyed before they can lift again. You cannot reach them from the air without waking the whole port, and you cannot reach them with a column without a stand-up battle the contract does not pay for. But you can reach them from the water. The basin sits at the head of a tidal estuary — kilometers of mudflat and reed channel that the harbor guard treats as a moat. It is too shallow for a ship and too open for a force, and the watchtowers face the sea, not the marsh. {NPC:intel-source} counts three heavy hulls in the graving docks, drives apart, unable to move or fight. The guard is thin: a harbor security detachment walking the quays and one light 'Mech lance on call at the port garrison. That report is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and a hull's repair can move forward in a single day. Your element goes in small and quiet, up the estuary at slack tide when the current is not fighting you, to place charges on hulls that sit blind in their cradles. The marsh cuts both ways. By night it is a road for anyone willing to wade it. By day it is open ground with no cover for kilometers, and a search will be closing across it. Planting the charges is the easy part — a stripped hull cannot dodge, shoot back, or do anything but burn. The hard part starts at the first blast, when {NPC:opfor-commander} floods the marsh with everything that can wade or fly. Your element will still be hours from safety, on foot, in the open, with the tide now turning against the way home. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, light and quiet. This is not a fight to win but a demolition raid to slip away from before the enemy can react. Go in on the slack tide, destroy the hulls in their cradles, and get off the flats before the search pins down your route. Stay too long and the same marsh that let you in becomes a trap that holds you for the enemy's 'Mech lance.

objectives.primary: Set and blow charges on at least two of the three DropShip hulls so they cannot lift, then get the element off the tidal flats before the port's search closes the marsh.
objectives.secondary: Destroy the basin's drive-rebuild shop and its stock of spare parts. A port that loses the hulls but keeps the parts recovers in months; a port that loses both takes years.
objectives.bonus: Recover or photograph the basin's repair manifest before you withdraw. It tells {EMPLOYER} which of {TARGET_FACTION}'s ships are down, where, and for how long across the whole theater.

complications.name: The Turning Tide
complications.text: The estuary lets you pass only at slack water. You come in while the current rests, but the moment the charges blow the tide is already turning. A turning tide in a reed channel pushes against you the whole way out, so the water that carried you in now slows you down.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track the tide state. After the charges blow, the element exfiltrates against the turning tide: movement through channel and mudflat hexes is slowed. An element that lingers at the docks past a set mark hits the full flood on the way out and slows further into the closing search.

complications.name: The First Blast
complications.text: Nothing wakes the port until the first charge goes off. There is no way to blow a hull quietly, so that first blast is what gives you away, and it starts the clock on the escape whether you are ready or not. The harbor goes from asleep to hunting in the time it takes a hull to catch fire.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The reaction timeline starts at the first detonation, not at insertion. Set all charges before any of them blow, or the search begins with hulls still un-mined. The element cannot both demolish slowly and exfiltrate clean.

complications.name: Open Flats by Day
complications.text: If the exfiltration runs long, daylight catches the element on the mudflats with nowhere to hide. The reeds at the channel edges give some cover, but the open flats give none. A light 'Mech or a spotter aircraft can pick out a moving figure across kilometers of mud.
complications.mechanicalEffect: If exfiltration runs into daylight, open-flat hexes give no concealment. The port's search 'Mech and any spotter get free detection rolls against elements crossing them, and a detected element draws the lance onto its line of retreat.

complications.name: The Repair State Lies
complications.text: Intelligence said three hulls are down. But the basin is a working yard, and a hull whose drive went back in yesterday can move today. The element may reach a cradle and find a ship further along in its repair than the manifest promised — guarded, and maybe even able to move under its own power.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a roll at the docks, one targeted hull is further along in repair than reported. It carries an active guard detail, and if it is not yet charged it may start moving out of the graving dock, forcing the element to choose between chasing it and finishing the others.

decisionPoints.name: Lighting the Hulls
decisionPoints.context: Three hulls, one tide, and an element too small to survive a fight. You can charge the hulls one at a time and slip out before any of them blow, charge them all and fire them together to be sure of the kills, or wreck the drive shop instead of the third hull. Each choice trades how much you destroy against how much head start you keep.

options.title: Sequence and Slip
advantages: Charges set quietly on every hull and the element well clear before the first blows — the maximum head start on the search
No firefight; the port wakes to find the damage already done and the doers gone
disadvantages: A long, patient setup spends the slack-tide window the exfiltration needs
A charge found or a guard stumbled into mid-setup blows the whole sequence early with hulls still un-mined
options.consequence: If the setup holds, you get the cleanest possible getaway. But the patience eats your tide window, and if you trip a guard partway you exfiltrate under a full search with the job half done.

costs.resource: the slack-tide window spent on a slow, complete setup before any charge fires
costs.risk: A guard stumbled into during the long setup starts the search with hulls un-charged and the tide already turning

options.title: Fire Them Together
advantages: Every charged hull blown at once — the surest destruction, nothing left half-mined for the yard to save
A single overwhelming blast sows confusion that buys the first minutes of the exfiltration
disadvantages: Simultaneous detonation means setting all charges before withdrawing — the element is still in the basin when they blow
The blast wave and fires across the whole basin make the docks themselves hazardous to cross on the way out
options.consequence: You guarantee the hulls, but you are still deep in the basin when every charge blows at once. You destroy them for certain and pay for it by being at the center of the blast.

costs.resource: the element committed inside the basin until the synchronized blast, with no early withdrawal
costs.risk: Caught in the basin by the blast and the fires, the element exfiltrates through its own destruction with the search already roused

options.title: Take the Drive Shop
advantages: Two hulls charged and the drive-rebuild shop wrecked instead of the third — the loss the yard cannot repair quickly
The shop sits inland of the cradles, a step closer to the exfiltration route off the flats
disadvantages: One hull left whole and able to be saved by the yard once the fires are out
The shop is the one structure in the basin with a standing watch — wrecking it risks the contact the cradles would not
options.consequence: You trade the third hull for the years it takes to rebuild a drive shop, and you accept the standing watch guarding it. You hurt the port's future more, at the cost of one hull left whole and a louder approach.

costs.resource: the third hull conceded whole in exchange for the drive shop's long-term destruction
costs.risk: The shop's standing watch makes contact before the charges are set, waking the basin early with two hulls still to confirm

entries.event: The first charge detonates; the harbor watch reports an explosion in the graving docks and the port garrison stands to.
{NPC:opfor-commander} releases the on-call light lance toward the basin and the harbor security detachment fans out along the quays and the marsh edge.
The search reaches the channel mouths the element used to come in; the tide has turned and the open flats are the only fast way out.
Spotter coverage extends over the estuary; an element still on the flats is being hunted from the air as well as the ground.
Daylight, or the closing of the last open channel, ends the window; an element not clear of the marsh by now is run down in the open.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The element must be off the tidal flats and clear of the marsh by T+24:00. By then the turning tide, the spreading search, and the coming daylight seal the estuary together. A team still on the flats is surrounded and captured, and a captured infiltrator hands {TARGET_FACTION} the sponsor the whole operation was meant to hide.

opforSketch.composition: A port-security response, light and reactive: one light 'Mech lance (20-35 tons) at Regular quality on call at the garrison, built for pursuit across open ground rather than a stand-up fight, plus the harbor security detachment (narrative infantry on the quays and in patrol craft, dressing the search) and possible spotter aircraft. The graving-dock hulls themselves are inert targets under repair, not combatants. One hull may carry an active guard detail if its repair is further along than reported.
opforSketch.behavior: Search-and-cordon doctrine: the lance does not defend the hulls — they are already lost — but races to cut the exfiltration routes off the flats and run the element down in the open, working with the harbor detachment to seal the channels. It presses hardest in daylight and on the open flats where its mobility tells; it will not wade deep into reed channels where a light 'Mech bogs.

forks.name: OPERATION EBB CHANNEL
forks.trigger: Hulls destroyed and the element exfiltrated clean off the flats, the sponsor unrevealed.
forks.consequence: The basin burns and {TARGET_FACTION} cannot prove who lit it. {EMPLOYER} presses the advantage with a follow-on against the crippled port's wider repair infrastructure while the yard is still counting its losses — a deeper strike now that the harbor's teeth are pulled.

forks.name: OPERATION DRAGNET
forks.trigger: The element was caught on the flats or compromised at the docks; the search has a line on it and the sponsor is exposed.
forks.consequence: The job is blown and the hunters know who sent the team. The next operation is a hasty extraction — get the surviving element off {WORLD} ahead of a port now actively hunting it and a garrison alerted to {EMPLOYER}'s hand. The fire was lit; now it is a fire to escape.

storyElementSeed: Someone lies flat in the reeds at the channel edge in the dark, counting the seconds between a tower searchlight's passes, a charge timer warm against the chest, the only sound the water working back down the mud.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Mine and destroy at least two of the three DropShip hulls in the graving docks, then get the team off the flats clean before the port's search closes the marsh — a quiet job, done quiet, with nothing left to say who did it.

merc.objectives.primary: Put at least two of the three hulls on the bottom of their cradles and get the team out before the search lines up the marsh. The contract pays for the hulls and the clean exit. A team caught on the flats loses the bonus, the fee, and the deniability all at once.

ESTUARY_LENGTH_KM.unit: km of estuary to the basin

inspiration: A captured leader is held at a mountaintop site reachable only by one road; a glider-borne snatch team lands on the summit itself, takes him before the guard can react, and is gone before a relief can climb.
skeleton: an aerospace-inserted snatch element must land directly onto an isolated high holding-site reachable by one ground road, seize a captured principal from a guard detail before it can organize, and lift him out before the road-bound relief can climb to the summit, where the whole problem is arriving on top of the objective instead of fighting up to it
title: OPERATION HIGH WINDOW
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} is holding a principal vouched for by {NPC:intel-source} — call the asset GREYLOCK — at a mountaintop site in {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}. {EMPLOYER} wants GREYLOCK out before an interrogation that has already begun finishes its work. The site is a former observation post on a high shoulder, walled and isolated. {TARGET_FACTION} chose it for one reason: there is exactly one road up, a switchback cut into the mountainside. A relief force can climb it, but an attacker would have to fight up it under fire the whole way. Take the road and you announce yourself hours before you reach the top, and the guard would move or kill GREYLOCK long before you crest the last bend. So you do not take the road. You come down on top of the post itself, dropped from aerospace onto the shoulder, landing on the objective instead of climbing to it. {NPC:intel-source} reads the guard as a reinforced light detail: a security lance and a platoon of infantry, Regular quality, comfortable behind their wall and their one road. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old, and a holding site's roster changes easily. The mountain works against you now. What makes the post safe from below makes the summit a trap with no second way out: once you are on the shoulder there is only the post, the cliff, and the one road — and the relief starts up that road the moment your DropShip is heard. The snatch is a race against that climb. You land, cross the wall, find GREYLOCK in the holding block before the guard organizes a defense, and lift off before the relief reaches the last switchback. If the relief reaches the gate, the snatch becomes a siege on a summit you cannot hold. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the valley garrison and keeps a reaction force at the foot of the road for exactly this. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Drop on the window, take GREYLOCK off the mountain, and be airborne before the road delivers the enemy — or be trapped on a summit with one road in, watching the relief climb it.

objectives.primary: Land directly on the mountaintop site, seize the principal GREYLOCK from the holding block before the guard can organize a defense or harm the asset, then lift off the shoulder before the road-bound relief reaches the summit.
objectives.secondary: Recover GREYLOCK's interrogation file, the record of what {TARGET_FACTION} has already pulled out. It tells {EMPLOYER} what was given up before the rescue and what must now be treated as compromised.
objectives.bonus: Take the site's signals officer alive along with GREYLOCK. This one person on the shoulder knows the garrison's wider holding network and the other names {TARGET_FACTION} has hidden on quiet mountaintops.

complications.name: The Climbing Relief
complications.text: The moment the DropShip is heard, {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force starts up the switchback road. It cannot arrive fast, and that slow climb is the whole reason the snatch is possible. But it is coming steadily, and every minute the element spends on the shoulder is another switchback the relief has climbed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track the relief's climb from insertion as a fixed countdown to the summit. The element must have GREYLOCK and be lifting before the countdown runs out. A relief that crests the last bend with the element still on the shoulder brings a heavy force into a fight on ground with no exit.

complications.name: The Hostage in the Block
complications.text: GREYLOCK is both the objective and the weak point. If the post is stormed, the guard's standing order is not to fight to the last. It is to kill the prisoner, because an asset who knows what was asked is worth more to {TARGET_FACTION} dead than to {EMPLOYER} alive. So the first moments on the shoulder are a race to reach GREYLOCK before a guard reaches the cell.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From insertion, a hidden clock runs on the guard reaching the holding block to kill the asset. Reaching and securing the block fast, or cutting the guard's internal communications first, saves GREYLOCK. A slow approach risks completing the rescue only to find the asset already dead.

complications.name: One Road, No Exit
complications.text: The summit has only the post, the cliff, and the one road. There is no way out overland: the element leaves by air or it does not leave. A DropShip circling to stay clear of the post's defenses is not on the ground when the element needs it. A DropShip on the ground is a fat target for anything the relief brings up the road.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Exfiltration is by air only. The lift ship's position is a live tradeoff: grounded for a fast pickup but exposed, or holding off for safety but adding minutes to the extraction. Damage to the lift ship from the relief's heavier weapons can strand the element on the shoulder.

complications.name: The Soft Roster
complications.text: A holding site's guard list is never as advertised. The post may hold more than the lance and platoon reported — a second detail rotated in, a heavier weapon mounted on the wall since the last look. The element lands committed, and learns the true count only once it is on the shoulder with the relief already climbing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a roll at insertion, the guard is reinforced beyond the reported strength — an extra security element or a wall-mounted heavy weapon covering the courtyard, lengthening the fight for the block and eating into the climb clock.

decisionPoints.name: Landing on the Window
decisionPoints.context: You are coming down on the shoulder, but how and where you land decides the snatch. Land hard inside the wall for speed and surprise; land outside it and breach the gate for control; or drop a cutting element onto the relief's road first to buy the shoulder more time. Each choice trades surprise, the asset's safety, and the climb clock differently.

options.title: Land Inside the Wall
advantages: Puts the element on top of the holding block in seconds — the fastest possible reach for GREYLOCK before the guard can act on the prisoner
Maximum surprise; the guard meets the assault inside its own courtyard before it can form a line
disadvantages: A landing inside a walled post is tight, hazardous ground, exposed to any heavy weapon on the wall the moment the ship flares
No control of the gate means the guard's outer elements can rally behind the element while it works the block
options.consequence: You give yourself the best odds on the asset, at the cost of a dangerous landing and an open perimeter. GREYLOCK is likely safe, but the element has to fight inward toward the block and outward against the rallying guard at the same time.

costs.resource: the lift ship exposed over the courtyard during a tight, hazardous insertion
costs.risk: A wall-mounted heavy weapon or a hard flare cripples the lift ship inside the wall — the element's only ride gone

options.title: Breach the Gate
advantages: Landing outside and taking the gate gives the element control of the post's one entrance and a secured perimeter
The lift ship stays clear of the wall's defenses during insertion, safer for the extraction it must perform
disadvantages: Breaching costs the minutes the climb clock is counting, and gives the guard those minutes to act on GREYLOCK
A contested gate is a chokepoint the guard can hold briefly, slowing the reach for the block
options.consequence: You trade speed to the asset for a controlled fight and a safer ship. The post is taken cleanly, but the delay at the gate is time the relief spends climbing and the guard spends reaching the cell.

costs.resource: time at the gate, against both the climb clock and the asset's safety clock
costs.risk: Minutes spent breaching let a guard reach GREYLOCK first — a clean assault that rescues no one

options.title: Cut the Road First
advantages: Dropping a cutting element onto a switchback below stalls or blocks the relief's climb, lengthening the shoulder's time
A road cut behind the relief's lead can strand its heavy elements below the block it falls
disadvantages: Splitting the force sends part of it down the mountain instead of at the block — fewer guns for the snatch itself
The cutting element on the road has its own exfiltration problem, and may have to be lifted out under fire separately
options.consequence: You buy the shoulder the time the snatch needs by dividing your weight; the post is taken against the clock you slowed, but a split force risks both halves being too light for what they meet.

costs.resource: demolition stores for the road cut and an element committed away from the block
costs.risk: A split force is caught in two places — the snatch under-gunned at the block, the cutters stranded on the road

entries.event: The lift ship is heard on approach; the post guard stands to, and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force starts up the switchback road from the valley floor.
The element is on the shoulder and inside or at the wall; the guard's internal order on the prisoner is given.
The relief is a third of the way up the road; the element should have GREYLOCK out of the block by now.
The relief's lead reaches the upper switchbacks within sight of the post; the lift ship must be loading or airborne.
The relief crests the shoulder. An element still on top is now in a fight on ground with one road and a cliff, no way out but the air it no longer controls.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The element must have GREYLOCK secured and be lifting off the shoulder before the relief crests the summit at T+15:00. A team caught on top by the relief is trapped on a mountaintop with no overland exit and a contested sky, and GREYLOCK is lost in the fight or back in the guard's hands.

opforSketch.composition: An isolated guard plus a road-bound relief: at the post, a light security lance (20-40 tons) at Regular quality behind a wall, with a narrative infantry platoon and possibly a wall-mounted heavy weapon. The relief climbing the road is a heavier reaction force — a medium 'Mech lance or company (40-65 tons), Regular, that cannot maneuver off the switchback. No armor on the summit; the ground is too broken and too high.
opforSketch.behavior: Isolated-holding doctrine: the post guard trusts its one road and its wall, and on being stormed shifts to dealing with the prisoner rather than a doomed defense of the courtyard. The relief grinds up the road at best safe speed, unable to flank, committed to reaching the summit; it does not turn back once started, betting that the climb is faster than the snatch.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET RANGE
forks.trigger: GREYLOCK lifted off the shoulder before the relief crested; the asset is out and the holding network's secret is loose.
forks.consequence: GREYLOCK is recovered, and the interrogation file or the signals officer has named the other quiet mountaintops where {TARGET_FACTION} keeps its prisoners. {EMPLOYER} moves on the network before it can be relocated — a follow-on snatch against a second holding site, now that the pattern is known.

forks.name: OPERATION CLOSED ROAD
forks.trigger: The relief crested with the element still on the shoulder, or GREYLOCK was lost in the block; the snatch became a fight on a summit with no exit.
forks.consequence: The element is pinned on the mountaintop with the relief on the shoulder and its sky contested. The next operation is to break it out — a relief of your own up the one road, or a fighting extraction off the summit before the trapped element is destroyed. The rescue became the thing that needs rescuing.

storyElementSeed: Wind on a bare summit, a holding-block door coming open, and a prisoner who flinches from the light not knowing yet whether the figures in the doorway are a worse interrogation or a way down the mountain.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Land on the mountaintop site, recover the asset GREYLOCK from the holding block before the guard can act, and lift clear before the relief climbs the road. One asset out, the account settled, before the bill arrives by the only road up.

merc.objectives.primary: Drop on the post, get GREYLOCK out of the block, and be airborne before the relief reaches the top. The fee is the asset breathing on your DropShip; a team trapped on the summit is a write-off the contract does not cover.

ROAD_CLIMB_MIN.unit: minutes for the relief to climb the road

inspiration: A raid on a lightly held coastal station to seize a working piece of the enemy's newest sensor gear and, just as important, a technician who knows how to run it, then withdraw by sea before the garrison reacts.
skeleton: a raid element must reach a lightly held coastal technical station, capture a working specimen of an enemy device AND a crew member who can operate it, and withdraw by water before the garrison reacts, where smashing the station is failure and the intelligence prize is worthless without the human who explains it
title: OPERATION GLASS HARVEST
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} has fielded a new sensor on {WORLD}: a deep-scan array on the coastal station at {DISTRICT} that is reading SLDF movements the command cannot keep losing. HPG STATION reports it is unlike anything in the known order of battle. {EMPLOYER} does not want it destroyed. {EMPLOYER} wants it taken — a working set, lifted out whole, brought home so the engineers can learn what makes it see. And because a captured machine no one can run is just a crate of riddles, the raid also wants the station's lead technician: the one person who knows the calibration the schematics will not show. {NPC:intel-source} reads the station as lightly held — a security lance and a section of armor, Regular quality, guarding a site chosen for its sea view and its quiet, not for a fight. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and a quiet station can be reinforced the week you arrive. The raid comes from the sea, lands on the shingle below the station, and climbs the cliff path while the garrison still treats the coast as its safe flank. The ground is tight: a narrow shelf of beach, a cliff with one path, and a station above it with open water at its back and the garrison's reaction force a coast-road drive away. The prize is fragile in two ways. The array must come out intact — a firefight in the equipment hall turns the thing you came for into scrap — and the technician has to come willing enough to be useful, which a wrecked station and a dead colleague do not encourage. {NPC:opfor-commander} holds the coastal sector and will send the reaction force the moment the station calls. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with the lift and recovery handled carefully. This is a theft, not a demolition. Get the array and the technician who runs it down the cliff and onto the boats before the reaction force arrives by road. Let the raid become a firefight in the station and you bring home only broken equipment and a dead technician — nothing the engineers can use.

objectives.primary: Seize a working specimen of the deep-scan array from the station's equipment hall, intact and movable, and withdraw it by sea before the garrison's reaction force arrives.
objectives.secondary: Capture the station's lead technician alive and cooperative, and extract them with the array. The hardware is just a riddle without the operator who can explain its calibration.
objectives.bonus: Recover the station's logged scan archive, the record of exactly what the array has already seen of SLDF movements. It tells the command what {TARGET_FACTION} learned before the device was taken.

complications.name: Fragile Glass
complications.text: The array is the prize, and it will not survive a fight. The deep-scan hardware is delicate and finely aligned, and it is worth nothing as a smoking ruin. Every weapon fired in or near the equipment hall risks wrecking the very thing you came to take. The raid has to lift a working machine out of a building it cannot let become a battlefield.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Weapons fire in or next to the equipment-hall structure rolls against the array's survival each time. A destroyed array fails the primary objective. The element must clear the hall by maneuver and close work, not firepower, to bring the specimen out whole.

complications.name: The Unwilling Expert
complications.text: The technician is a person, not a component. Taken at gunpoint over a colleague's body, they are a sullen prisoner who will give the engineers nothing useful; taken cleanly, separated from the fight, they are an asset who can be persuaded that cooperation beats the alternative. How the station is taken decides what kind of expert comes home.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The technician's cooperation is tracked against the violence of the station's capture. Heavy collateral damage or technical-staff casualties degrade the secondary objective from a cooperative asset to a hostile one; a clean, contained capture preserves their usefulness.

complications.name: The Sea at Its Back
complications.text: The station's only retreat for the raid is the water it came from. The beach shelf is narrow, the cliff path is single-file, and the lift must take the array, the technician, and the element back down to the boats under whatever weather the coast offers. A rising sea or a contested beach turns the clean withdrawal into a scramble on a shrinking shingle.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Exfiltration funnels through the single cliff path to the beach. Track the sea state and the beach as a chokepoint; the array and the prisoner slow the descent, and a reaction force reaching the cliff top before the element is down catches it strung on the path.

complications.name: The Quiet Station Wakes
complications.text: The station was chosen for quiet, but quiet is not the same as undefended, and {TARGET_FACTION} may have grown nervous about its valuable new sensor. The garrison could be larger than the last look showed: a second security element rotated in, or a heavier piece on the cliff road now that the array has proven its worth.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a roll at the cliff top, the station's guard is reinforced beyond the report, lengthening the fight for the equipment hall and threatening the survival of the fragile array in a longer engagement.

decisionPoints.name: Taking the Station
decisionPoints.context: A working machine and a willing man, out of a building you cannot shoot up, before the road delivers the garrison. You can move in quiet and surgical, hit hard and fast to own the station before it reacts, or seal the cliff road first to buy the equipment hall its delicate work. Each answer trades the prize's safety against the clock.

options.title: Quiet and Surgical
advantages: Minimal fire near the equipment hall — the best protection for the fragile array and the cleanest capture of the technician
A contained entry keeps the station's call for help late and the prisoner cooperative
disadvantages: A careful, low-violence entry is slow, and slow against a garrison that may wake at any moment
Surgical work demands the guard be neutralized quietly — a single alarm turns the delicate plan into the brawl it was meant to avoid
options.consequence: You give the array and the technician their best odds, at the cost of speed. The prize comes out whole if the quiet holds, but a tripped alarm leaves you doing delicate work under a reaction clock you no longer control.

costs.resource: time spent on a careful, low-fire entry to protect the array and the prisoner
costs.risk: An alarm during the slow approach forces the fragile extraction under a reaction clock already running

options.title: Hard and Fast
advantages: Overwhelms the guard before it can organize or call — the station is yours in minutes
Speed banks the most time against the reaction force on the coast road
disadvantages: A violent assault near the equipment hall is the surest way to wreck the very array you came for
A man taken in the middle of a firefight, his colleagues dead, is a prisoner who tells the engineers nothing
options.consequence: You own the station fast and keep the most withdrawal time, but you put both prizes at the greatest risk. Sweeping the station clean while wrecking the array and souring the technician means winning the fight and losing the point of the raid.

costs.resource: the array's survival and the prisoner's cooperation staked on a violent, fast capture
costs.risk: A firefight in the hall destroys the array and sours the technician — speed bought with the mission's whole point

options.title: Seal the Cliff Road
advantages: Blocking or covering the coast road delays the reaction force, buying the equipment hall the time for delicate work
A sealed road lets the rest of the element take the station at the careful pace the array needs
disadvantages: Splitting weight onto the road leaves fewer guns to take the station and cover the cliff path
The blocking element has its own withdrawal to manage once the array is down on the beach
options.consequence: You buy the careful capture the time it wants by holding the garrison off, at the price of a divided force; the prize comes out whole if the road holds, but the blockers must then break clean themselves.

costs.resource: an element committed to the coast road and the stores to block it
costs.risk: The road element is cut off from the beach when the reaction force arrives in strength, stranded above the cliff

entries.event: The element reaches the station and the guard is engaged or alerted; the station signals the coastal garrison.
{NPC:opfor-commander} releases the reaction force down the coast road toward the station.
The array should be out of the equipment hall and moving to the cliff path by now; the technician secured.
The reaction force nears the station's landward approaches; the element should be on the beach loading the boats.
The reaction force reaches the cliff top. An element still ashore is caught with the prize on a narrow beach under fire from above.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The array and the technician must be off the beach and onto the water by T+22:00, when the reaction force reaches the cliff top. An element still on the shingle is pinned against the sea with the fragile prize, and a raid that loses the array or the technician in that fight has smashed a station for nothing.

opforSketch.composition: A light technical-station guard plus a road-bound reaction force: at the station, a security lance (25-45 tons) at Regular quality with a supporting armor section of 2-4 vehicles (Scorpion and Vedette behavior), guarding a site built for quiet. The reaction force on the coast road is a heavier element — a medium lance or company, Regular, with armor support, committed to the single coast road. The station's value may have drawn extra strength since the last look.
opforSketch.behavior: Light-guard doctrine at a technical site: the station guard defends a perimeter it does not expect to be tested and calls for help early. The reaction force drives the coast road at speed to relieve the station, unable to flank off the road; it presses to reach the cliff top before the raiders can withdraw, knowing the prize is on a narrow beach with one path.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR SIGHT
forks.trigger: The array and its technician are off the water intact and cooperative; the SLDF will learn what {TARGET_FACTION} could see.
forks.consequence: The engineers have the device and the man who runs it, and the scan archive shows exactly what was compromised. {EMPLOYER} acts on the recovered intelligence with a strike against the network the array was feeding — moving now, while {TARGET_FACTION} does not yet know its eyes have been stolen rather than merely blinded.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN LENS
forks.trigger: The array was wrecked in the fight, or the element was caught on the beach with the prize; the theft became a brawl.
forks.consequence: The raid did not bring home what it came for, and {TARGET_FACTION} now knows the SLDF wants its new sensor badly enough to bleed for it. The next operation is to break the surviving element clear of the coast and off {WORLD} before the alerted garrison runs it down — the harvest spoiled, the escape all that is left.

storyElementSeed: A technician's workbench in a sea-lit hall, a half-calibrated array humming on the bench, and a stranger in unfamiliar armor saying quietly that the man can come and keep his hands, or stay and lose the work of years.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Lift a working set of the deep-scan array out of the station's equipment hall, whole and movable, and get it off the coast before the reaction force closes — bring home the machine, not the wreckage.

COAST_ROAD_KM.unit: km of coast road for the reaction force

inspiration: Cheap, expendable hulls are sent burning into a crowded enemy anchorage at night to break its order and scatter its ships, turning a tight formation into chaos for the cost of a few vessels no one will miss.
skeleton: a force must drive a handful of cheap expendable units into a massed enemy staging area to panic and scatter a tight formation before it can sortie, where the attackers' own units are the spent currency, the goal is disorder and delay rather than destruction, and the real fight is whether the scattered enemy reforms before the disruption pays off
title: OPERATION FIRE SHIP
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} has massed a strike force in the staging grounds at {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}: DropShips, armor, and 'Mechs packed tight on the hardstand, fueling and arming for an offensive. {EMPLOYER} cannot meet that offensive head-on and cannot let it lift on schedule. So {EMPLOYER} will not meet it head-on. {EMPLOYER} will scatter it. The plan is old and cheap. A handful of expendable units — worn-out 'Mechs at the end of their service, salvage hulls patched just enough to walk, and vehicles loaded with everything that burns — drive straight into the packed staging area at night to set its fuel and ammunition alight and panic the tight formation into a stampede. {NPC:intel-source} reads the staging grounds as a dense, fuel-heavy laager guarded by a perimeter screen and a ready reaction company, with the bulk of the force buttoned up and unready for a fight on its own hardstand. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and a staging force lifts on its own clock. The flat ground is the whole opportunity. The same flat that lets {TARGET_FACTION} pack its force tight lets the fire spread and the panic run. A dense formation has nowhere to scatter to in a hurry, and a few burning hulls among the fuel bladders turn order into chaos. The expendable units are meant to be spent. They get in among the ships, do their damage, and are lost. What matters is not bringing them home but the hours of disorder they buy while {TARGET_FACTION} sorts out a scattered, half-burned force. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the staging grounds and will react fast to save the offensive. The whole question is whether the formation reforms before the chaos has cost it its schedule. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with the expendable element counted as spent the moment it goes in. Light the laager and scatter the strike force, or watch a formation shrug off your fire, reform, and lift on time.

objectives.primary: Drive the expendable element into the massed staging area, set its fuel and ammunition stores alight, and scatter the packed formation badly enough to break its offensive timetable and delay the sortie past the point it matters to {EMPLOYER}.
objectives.secondary: Cripple an outsized share of the heavy lift — the DropShips and assault 'Mechs the formation cannot quickly replace. Then the delay is not just hours but weight gone from the offensive for good.
objectives.bonus: Pull the crews of the expendable element out after their run rather than losing them with the hulls. This costs {EMPLOYER} machines but not people.

complications.name: The Spent Units
complications.text: The expendable units are not coming back, and planning as if they might wrecks the whole idea. They are meant to get in among the ships and be lost. Once committed, they are gone, and the only question is how much chaos they cause before they burn. Hold them back to save them and you get neither the units nor the chaos.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The expendable element is a one-way force: its destruction is expected, not a loss condition. Disruption is scored by the chaos it sows and the stores it ignites before it is lost, not by whether it survives. Holding it back from the densest packing reduces the disruption it can cause.

complications.name: The Reforming Formation
complications.text: Scattering a force is not the same as destroying it. The instant the fires start, {NPC:opfor-commander} works to reform: rallying scattered elements, fighting the fires, and sorting the panic back into order. The chaos fades with every minute that passes. The operation pays off only if the formation cannot reassemble before its schedule is broken.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a reform clock. From the start of the chaos, the formation recovers order in steps. Each store ignited and each lift asset crippled lengthens the time it needs to reform. If the formation reassembles before the disruption threshold, the offensive lifts on time and the operation fails despite the damage done.

complications.name: The Fuel-Heavy Ground
complications.text: The staging ground is packed with fuel and munitions, which is what makes the fire ship work and what makes the whole area lethal to be in. A fire among the bladders does not stay where it is lit — it spreads, cooks off ammunition, and turns the hardstand into a place no one, attacker or defender, can cross safely once it takes hold.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Ignited fuel and ammunition stores spread fire and cook-off hazards across adjacent hexes on a growing radius, dangerous to all units. The expendable element exploits this; the extraction element and the defender's reaction force both have to reckon with a hardstand that becomes impassable in patches.

complications.name: The Ready Company
complications.text: Not the whole force is buttoned up. {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps a reaction company at readiness on the perimeter, the one part of the formation that can fight at once, and it will move to contain the raid and shepherd the panicked elements back into order. It cannot stop the fires alone, but it can hunt the raiders and shorten the chaos.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The ready reaction company engages the raid from the start, working to contain the disruption and cover the reforming formation. It fights to limit the chaos rather than to win outright, and pulling it into a pursuit of the extraction element draws it away from the reform effort.

decisionPoints.name: Driving the Laager
decisionPoints.context: The expendables go in, but where and how decides what the disruption costs the enemy. Aim them at the fuel for the widest fire; aim them at the heavy lift for lasting damage; or hold a real element back to deepen the panic and cover the crews' extraction. Each answer trades the spread of the chaos against the weight of the loss and the lives of the crews.

options.title: Aim for the Fuel
advantages: Striking the fuel bladders spreads fire across the widest area — the most chaos and the longest reform clock
A burning hardstand panics the densest part of the formation and denies it the ground to rally on
disadvantages: Fire spreads where it will; it may consume the lighter screen and spare the heavy lift the offensive actually depends on
A general conflagration is hard to steer toward the targets whose loss would matter most
options.consequence: You buy the most disorder and the longest delay, but the damage falls where the fire runs rather than where it would hurt; the schedule breaks, but the heavy weight may survive to lift later.

costs.resource: the expendables spent on the fuel stores for maximum spread rather than aimed at specific weight
costs.risk: A wide fire scatters the force but spares the assault lift — delay won, lasting loss missed

options.title: Aim for the Heavy Lift
advantages: Driving the expendables onto the DropShips and assault 'Mechs cripples the weight the offensive cannot replace
Damage that lasts beyond the delay — the offensive lifts later and lighter, if at all
disadvantages: The heavy lift is the best-guarded part of the laager; the expendables burn reaching it and may be stopped short
Concentrating on the heavy assets sows less general panic — a tighter, smaller fire the formation reforms around faster
options.consequence: You go for lasting damage at the cost of wide chaos. Cripple the lift and the offensive is gutted, but a tight, contained strike is one the enemy recovers its order around faster.

costs.resource: the expendables driven through the heaviest guard to reach the lift, likely stopped short of full effect
costs.risk: A strike contained around the heavy lift reforms fast — the lasting damage done but the schedule barely dented

options.title: Hold a Real Element Back
advantages: A genuine element kept in reserve deepens and prolongs the panic after the expendables are spent, and can extract their crews
Keeps the volunteers alive and adds real combat weight to shepherd the chaos at the decisive moment
disadvantages: The held-back element is real strength risked in a fight meant to be fought by the expendable hulls
Lingering to extract crews and prolong the panic keeps your force in a hardstand that is turning into a firestorm
options.consequence: You make the disruption last and bring the crews home, but you stake real units on staying in a burning laager longer than the expendables alone would have; the payoff is greater and so is the exposure.

costs.resource: a real element committed to the laager beyond the expendables, exposed to the fire and the reaction company
costs.risk: The held-back element is caught in the spreading fire or the reaction company's containment — real weight lost to a one-way mission

entries.event: The expendable element penetrates the staging perimeter and the first fuel stores go up; the laager alarms and the formation scrambles.
Fire spreads through the packed hardstand; {NPC:opfor-commander} commits the ready reaction company to contain the raid and begins fighting the fires.
The panic is at its height — the disruption window is open; the heavy lift's fate is decided in these minutes.
The reaction company and the fire teams begin restoring order; the reform clock runs against the disruption already sown.
The formation reassembles enough to assess its schedule; if the disruption held past this mark, the offensive timetable is broken.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The chaos must break the offensive's timetable before the formation reforms by T+20:00. A force that reassembles in order with its schedule intact lifts on time despite the fires, and the expendables — along with any real weight risked with them — are spent for a delay that never came.

opforSketch.composition: A massed staging force, mostly unready: the bulk a packed formation of mixed 'Mechs and armor (all weights) buttoned up and fueling, not a fighting line. The active threat is a ready reaction company — a medium-to-heavy 'Mech company (45-75 tons) at Regular quality with an armor element — held at the perimeter for exactly this. The expendable raiders face the screen and this company, not the whole laager, which is busy not burning.
opforSketch.behavior: Staging-laager doctrine under attack: the bulk of the force fights the fires and tries to reform rather than to engage; the ready reaction company moves to contain the raid, shepherd panicked elements, and shorten the chaos. It does not pursue recklessly into the spreading fire and prioritizes restoring the formation's order over hunting every raider, because the offensive's schedule is the thing it is really defending.

forks.name: OPERATION SCATTERED ASH
forks.trigger: The formation was scattered past reforming in time; the offensive's timetable is broken and the strike force lifts late and disordered, if at all.
forks.consequence: The blow {EMPLOYER} could not meet head-on will not land on schedule, and a half-burned formation is a tempting target. {EMPLOYER} exploits the disorder with a strike against the scattered, weakened elements before they can fully reassemble — pressing the advantage the fire ships bought.

forks.name: OPERATION REFORMED LINE
forks.trigger: The formation contained the fires and reformed in time; the offensive's schedule survived and the expendables were spent for little.
forks.consequence: The strike force is shaken but intact and lifting near its schedule, and now it is coming. The next operation is a defense — meet the offensive the fire ships failed to stop, on ground of {EMPLOYER}'s choosing, with the disruption having bought only a few hours' grace. The cheap plan failed; the expensive fight begins.

storyElementSeed: A volunteer in a worn-out 'Mech at the line of departure, running through a checklist that does not include coming back, watching the packed lights of the enemy laager and waiting for the word to drive in.

is-marik.objectives.primary: Drive the expendable element into the massed staging force, fire its stores, and scatter the formation badly enough to break the offensive's timetable. Cheap hulls traded for an enemy's schedule, and worth every one of them if it holds.

merc.objectives.primary: Run the expendable hulls into the laager, light the fuel, and scatter the formation past reforming on time. The contract buys the delay, not the hulls — they were written off before the line of departure.

inspiration: A liberation force lands to retake a usurped capital world held by a former ally who turned coat and dug in behind the very planetary defenses he was trusted to man — and who holds the population as his shield.
skeleton: the player's company runs one urban slice of a larger liberation of a usurped capital held by a former ally entrenched behind the defenses he was trusted with, where the defender uses the loyal population as cover, the liberators must fight a betrayer who knows their own doctrine, and the prize is a city freed rather than flattened
title: OPERATION TRUE NORTH
situation: {WORLD} was loyal, and the man who holds it now was trusted. He was a former ally who turned, seized the capital in {DISTRICT}, and dug in behind the planetary defenses he had been given to protect it. The liberation is a whole campaign; your company runs one slice of it. The main force has the orbit and the outer city. Your task is one district of the capital itself, where the betrayer's people are dug in among a population that never stopped being loyal and is now a hostage to the defense. {NPC:intel-source} reads your district as held by a reinforced company of the usurper's troops, Regular-to-Veteran quality, fighting from prepared urban positions. They use the civil infrastructure — the shelters, the hospitals, the packed residential towers — as cover that your rules of engagement will not let you simply blast through. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old, and a defender who knows he is losing fortifies fast. This is a hard fight for one reason: the enemy was trained the same way you were. He knows the doctrine you will use and has built his defense to punish exactly the textbook assault. And he hides among people who are on your side and will die if you fight the way the ground invites. Your prize is the district freed and standing with its people alive. You want the capital liberated, not flattened, because a city reduced to rubble to save it is a win for the usurper, not for you. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands your district's defense and will trade the population's safety for time without hesitation, daring you to be the one who brings the towers down. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, the player's company as one part of the larger liberation. Free the district and keep it whole, or fight the fight the betrayer wants and win a graveyard.

objectives.primary: Clear the assigned capital district of the usurper's forces and secure it for the liberation. Break the prepared urban defense while keeping the district's loyal population and its critical infrastructure mostly intact.
objectives.secondary: Take the district's defense headquarters and its commander's records. They prove who turned, who was coerced, and which of the usurper's troops might be won back rather than fought to the last.
objectives.bonus: Secure the district's shelters and hospitals before the defense can turn them into final strongpoints. This denies {NPC:opfor-commander} his human shields and saves the people sheltering there from the last stand.

complications.name: He Knows Your Doctrine
complications.text: The defender trained where you trained. He knows the approach the manual recommends, the way a company is supposed to fight through a city, and the support you expect to call on. His defense is built to punish the textbook and turn the doctrine you trust into a trap. Fight him by the book and you fight him exactly the way he prepared for.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The defense anticipates standard assault patterns: prepared positions cover the doctrinally obvious approaches and support a counter to the expected maneuver. Unconventional approaches that deviate from the manual catch the defense off its prepared ground; predictable ones walk into it.

complications.name: The Loyal Hostages
complications.text: The people in this district are on your side, and the defender is using them as cover. He fights from among the residential towers and the shelters, knowing your rules will not let you flatten a building full of loyal civilians to root out a platoon. Every position he holds among them is a question: how much of the city do you break to take it back?
complications.mechanicalEffect: Heavy or area fire against occupied civil structures carries a collateral track with a hard ceiling tied to the rules of engagement. Crossing it voids the keep-it-whole condition of the primary, converts a SUCCESS toward COMPROMISED, and feeds the usurper's narrative regardless of the tactical result.

complications.name: Fast Fortification
complications.text: A defender who knows he is losing the planet does not husband his effort. {NPC:opfor-commander} fortifies the district as fast as he can — wiring buildings, blocking streets, turning every delay into a deeper defense. The district you assault tomorrow is harder than the one scouted today.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The defense's prepared positions deepen over the engagement: streets blocked, buildings rigged, strongpoints linked. A slow, methodical advance gives the defender time to harden ground ahead of it; pace traded against the collateral risk of a faster push.

complications.name: Troops Who Might Turn Back
complications.text: Not everyone under the usurper turned willingly. Some of the troops in the district were coerced, or followed orders they now regret, and a few might lay down arms if given the chance rather than the muzzle. Telling the committed traitor from the reluctant conscript in the middle of a firefight is its own problem, and getting it wrong wastes lives on both sides.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On a roll at contact with a defending element, that element is wavering and may surrender if offered the chance rather than pressed to destruction; accepting surrenders preserves troops who feed the secondary's intelligence and eases the wider liberation, while treating all defenders as committed costs those lives and that information.

decisionPoints.name: Freeing the District
decisionPoints.context: A district full of loyal people, a defender who knows your manual, and a city you must not wreck. You can go by the book and trade collateral risk for speed, work an unconventional line the defender did not prepare, or fight to take the shelters first and deny him his shields. Each answer trades the city's safety, the clock, and your own losses differently.

options.title: By the Book, Fast
advantages: The doctrinally direct assault is the quickest way to clear the district before the defense deepens
Concentrated, supported advance brings the most weight to bear at the decisive points
disadvantages: It is exactly the assault the betrayer prepared to punish — into his prepared positions and his counter
The fastest, heaviest fighting in an inhabited district is the surest way to run the collateral track and break the city
options.consequence: You clear the ground fast and on familiar terms, straight into the defense built to meet it; speed and weight at the price of walking his trap and risking the towers you came to save.

costs.resource: the assault driven by the manual into the defender's prepared ground and counter
costs.risk: The textbook approach meets the textbook trap, and the heavy fighting among the towers breaks the city it frees

options.title: Work an Unconventional Line
advantages: An approach off the doctrinal axis catches the defense away from its prepared positions and its counter
Fighting on ground the betrayer did not rig spares more of the city and more of your company
disadvantages: The unconventional line is slower and harder to support, ground the manual avoided for reasons
A clever route that goes wrong leaves the company strung in bad ground without the support a doctrinal axis would have
options.consequence: You unsettle the defense and protect the city by refusing the fight he prepared, at the cost of speed and sure support; done well it unhinges him, done badly it strands you off the map he and you both know.

costs.resource: time and sure support traded for an approach the defender did not prepare
costs.risk: An unconventional line gone wrong leaves the company unsupported in bad ground the manual avoided

options.title: Take the Shelters First
advantages: Securing the shelters and hospitals early denies {NPC:opfor-commander} his human shields and final strongpoints
Saves the most vulnerable population and removes the collateral leverage from the rest of the fight
disadvantages: Diverting to the shelters first delays the clearance of the district and gives the defense time to deepen
The shelters may already be held — taking them is a delicate fight among packed civilians of its own
options.consequence: You pull the hostages out from under the defense before clearing it, trading time and a hard delicate fight for a city you can then take without the towers held against you; the humane line is also the slow one.

costs.resource: the advance diverted to the shelters first, conceding time to the deepening defense
costs.risk: A defense given time while you clear the shelters hardens the rest of the district into a longer, costlier fight

entries.event: The company enters the assigned district; the usurper's defense stands to in its prepared urban positions and the population goes to ground.
{NPC:opfor-commander} commits his reserve to the threatened approaches and begins pulling elements into the shelters as strongpoints.
The defense deepens — streets blocked, buildings rigged; the collateral picture forms wherever the fighting is heaviest.
The defense headquarters is in reach if the advance held its pace; the wavering elements decide whether to fight on or fold.
The district is cleared and secured, or the fight congeals among the towers; the wider liberation's timetable depends on this slice being done.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The district must be cleared and secured by T+24:00 to hold the liberation's timetable, and it must be taken mostly whole. A district freed as rubble, or a fight left stalled among the towers, hands the usurper the only victory left to him: proof that liberation costs the loyal more than the betrayal did.

opforSketch.composition: A turncoat's prepared urban defense: a reinforced company of the usurper's troops (all weights, 30-85 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality fighting from prepared positions, supported by a street-fighting armor element (SRM and short-range behavior) and fixed emplacements woven into the civil infrastructure. The defenders are trained in the liberators' own doctrine. Some elements are coerced conscripts who may waver; the core is committed.
opforSketch.behavior: Betrayer's-defense doctrine: hold the prepared ground that punishes the textbook assault, use the loyal population and the shelters as cover the liberators' rules will not let them blast, and trade civilian safety for time without hesitation. The committed core fights hard and fortifies as it goes; wavering elements may fold if offered the chance, but {NPC:opfor-commander} counts on the liberators being unwilling to win the way he is willing to lose.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN SLATE
forks.trigger: The district was freed and kept whole, its people alive and its defense broken; the liberation advances on the betrayer's core.
forks.consequence: The district stands liberated and intact, and its captured records name the usurper's network across the capital. The liberation presses inward toward the seat the betrayer holds, and your company takes the next slice — the fight closing on the man who turned, district by district.

forks.name: OPERATION HELD GROUND
forks.trigger: The district could not be cleared, or was wrecked taking it; the slice stalled and the wider timetable slipped.
forks.consequence: The advance stalls in the district and the betrayer makes the most of it, deepening his hold and his narrative that liberation only brings ruin. The next operation is to hold the ground won and contain the defense while the main force reworks its plan — the liberation checked, the city still partly his. The campaign bends; the betrayer buys time.

storyElementSeed: A family in a stairwell shelter listening to 'Mech footfalls in the street above, unsure whether the soldiers coming are the ones who turned or the ones come to undo it, holding very still either way.

inspiration: A deep multi-axis offensive races into enemy territory faster than its own supply can follow, and must reach its objective and win before the advance outruns its fuel and ammunition and culminates short of the goal.
skeleton: the player's company spearheads one axis of a deep multi-pronged offensive that has outrun its own logistics, where the objective must be reached and held before the supply tail catches up or the whole thrust culminates and stalls in enemy depth, and the crux is whether to push the exhausted spearhead one bound further or consolidate before it breaks
title: OPERATION FAR BOUND
situation: {EMPLOYER}'s offensive into {TARGET_FACTION}'s territory on {WORLD} has gone fast and deep — too fast. Three axes drove into the interior of {DISTRICT} to break the defense before it could set. They have, but the supply tail has not kept up, so the whole thrust is running on what it can carry. Your company spearheads the deepest axis, and you are close to the objective: a road junction and supply town that, once taken and held, cuts the defender's lateral movement and makes the breakthrough permanent. {NPC:intel-source} reads the objective as held by a defending battalion-slice fighting to buy time for its own reinforcements, Regular-to-Veteran quality, dug into the town and the junction. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old, and a defender racing his own clock fortifies while he waits. The ground is fast to cross but hard to supply across: open interior with long, exposed roads back to the railhead. The further you push, the longer and thinner the line your fuel and ammunition come up. The real danger is not the next fight. It is the fight after, when the spearhead has spent its supplies reaching the objective and none has arrived to let it hold. An offensive that outruns its supply does not lose a battle — it culminates. It reaches a point where it cannot attack again, cannot be resupplied in time, and cannot pull back fast enough to escape, and it stalls deep in enemy territory where the defender's gathering reinforcements catch it. The decision under the whole operation is the oldest one in a deep advance: push the exhausted spearhead one bound further and take the prize now, or halt short and risk the moment passing while the defender sets. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the objective and is trading ground for the time his reinforcements need. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, the spearhead of one axis. Take the junction before you culminate, or stall deep in enemy territory with empty racks and his reserves arriving.

objectives.primary: Seize the road junction and supply town at the head of the axis and hold it, cutting {TARGET_FACTION}'s lateral movement and making the breakthrough permanent, before the spearhead runs out of fuel and ammunition.
objectives.secondary: Capture the town's fuel and ammunition stocks intact. That turns the objective into a forward supply point the spearhead can hold from, instead of a prize it cannot keep.
objectives.bonus: Take and hold the road connecting to a neighboring thrust, so the breakthrough is a solid front rather than an exposed finger the defender can pinch off.

complications.name: The Culmination Point
complications.text: The spearhead is running on what it carries, and that is nearly gone. There is a point coming when the company can no longer attack, cannot be resupplied in time, and cannot pull back fast enough to escape the gathering reserves. Reaching the objective with empty racks is not a win. It means arriving spent, on the enemy's ground, with nothing left.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track the spearhead's fuel and ammunition as a resource that drains across the operation. Each major action draws it down. Past a threshold the company cannot keep attacking and may be unable to hold or withdraw. The objective must be taken and supply secured before that point, or the hold fails by exhaustion.

complications.name: The Lengthening Supply Line
complications.text: Every bound deeper stretches the line back to the railhead thinner, and a thin line is easy to cut. The supply that does come up runs a long, exposed road through ground where the defender's bypassed elements still lurk. A single strike back there starves the spearhead at the front.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Resupply arrives slowly and unreliably along the lengthening line. On a roll between phases, the supply road is cut to the rear, delaying or denying a resupply increment and pushing the spearhead faster toward culmination.

complications.name: The Defender's Clock
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} is not trying to win the battle at the junction. He is trying to last until his reinforcements arrive, trading the town's ground for the hours they need. The longer the spearhead takes to force the objective, the closer those reserves come — and a spearhead that arrives exhausted just as fresh defenders do is a spearhead destroyed in enemy depth.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A defender reinforcement clock runs against the operation; if the objective is not taken and consolidated before it expires, fresh enemy weight arrives to contest the exhausted spearhead, raising the FAILURE fork's threat and the risk of the company being cut off.

complications.name: Exposed Flanks
complications.text: A deep spearhead has open flanks by definition — it ran ahead of the line on either side, and the ground it bypassed is full of defenders it went around rather than through. Those elements can close on the axis's flanks as it slows near the objective, threatening to pinch off the finger the company has driven into enemy territory.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Bypassed enemy elements may close on the spearhead's flanks as it nears the objective, especially if it slows; linking with a neighboring thrust (the bonus) closes the flank, while pushing alone leaves it open to being cut off.

decisionPoints.name: The Last Bound
decisionPoints.context: The objective is one bound away and the spearhead is nearly spent. Push now and take it before you culminate; consolidate short and secure your supply before the final effort; or split off to link the neighboring axis and close your flank first. Each answer trades the prize, the company's endurance, and the open flank differently.

options.title: Push the Last Bound Now
advantages: Takes the junction before the defender's reinforcements arrive and before the spearhead fully culminates
Seizing the town's intact supply stocks could refuel the spearhead and solve the exhaustion at a stroke
disadvantages: Spends the last of the fuel and ammunition on the assault, leaving nothing if the stocks are destroyed or denied
An exhausted spearhead that takes the town may lack the strength to hold it against the arriving reserves
options.consequence: You go for the prize while the going is barely possible, betting the spearhead's last reserve on taking the supply that would sustain it; win and the breakthrough is made, lose and you culminate in the town with the reserves at the gate.

costs.resource: the spearhead's last fuel and ammunition spent on the final assault, refilled only if the stocks are taken intact
costs.risk: An exhausted spearhead takes the town and cannot hold it — culmination at the objective with the reserves arriving

options.title: Consolidate Short
advantages: Halting to let supply catch up rebuilds the spearhead's endurance before the decisive effort
A consolidated company that then attacks has the reserve to both take the junction and hold it
disadvantages: The pause gives {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reinforcements time to arrive and the defense time to deepen
Consolidating short of the objective on exposed ground invites the bypassed flanking elements to close
options.consequence: You trade the moment for endurance, betting that a stronger attack later beats a weak one now; the spearhead holds together, but the prize may be far harder to take once the defender's reserves are in it.

costs.resource: the initiative and the defender's clock traded for the time to resupply and consolidate
costs.risk: The pause lets the reserves arrive and the defense set — the junction taken later against far heavier weight, if at all

options.title: Link the Neighboring Axis First
advantages: Closing the flank with the neighboring thrust secures the spearhead against being pinched off
A continuous front shares supply and weight, easing the exhaustion and the exposure both
disadvantages: Diverting to link sideways spends time and the last fuel on something other than the objective
The connecting road may be contested — the link is a fight of its own, not a free maneuver
options.consequence: You secure the finger before driving it deeper, trading the direct push for a safer base to attack from; the spearhead is no longer alone, but the objective waits while you spend endurance closing the flank.

costs.resource: fuel and time spent linking sideways rather than driving on the objective
costs.risk: A contested link spends the spearhead's reserve without taking the objective — exhausted and still short of the prize

entries.event: The spearhead closes on the road junction; the defending slice stands to in the town and the junction, fighting to buy time.
The assault on the objective is joined; the spearhead's fuel and ammunition draw down hard in the fight for the town.
The defender trades ground for the junction's approaches; the spearhead nears its culmination point as the racks run low.
{NPC:opfor-commander}'s reinforcements approach the area; the town's supply stocks must be in hand by now to sustain the hold.
The junction is taken and consolidated, or the spearhead has culminated short; the breakthrough is made permanent or stalls in enemy depth.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The road junction must be taken, its supply secured, and the position consolidated by T+24:00, before the spearhead culminates and the defender's reinforcements arrive. A company that reaches the objective with empty racks as fresh enemy weight closes is destroyed deep in enemy territory, and the offensive stalls short of the prize that would have made it permanent.

opforSketch.composition: A defending slice fighting for time: a battalion-slice of mixed 'Mechs (40-80 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality dug into the supply town and the junction, supported by an armor element and fixed positions, trading ground deliberately. Behind it, a reinforcement element races to arrive — fresh medium-to-heavy weight that contests the exhausted spearhead if it arrives before the objective is consolidated. Bypassed enemy elements haunt the spearhead's flanks and rear.
opforSketch.behavior: Delaying-defense doctrine against a deep thrust: the junction slice trades the town's ground for time, fortifying as it waits and never overcommitting, betting that the spearhead culminates before the objective falls. The arriving reinforcements aim to catch the spearhead exhausted; the bypassed elements interdict the supply line and threaten the flanks. The whole defense is a clock the attacker is racing, not a wall to break.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRM JUNCTION
forks.trigger: The junction was taken and held, its supply secured, before the spearhead culminated; the breakthrough is permanent.
forks.consequence: The junction is held and the captured stocks have the spearhead breathing again, the breakthrough made permanent and the defender's lateral movement cut. {EMPLOYER} pushes the advantage from the new forward base, your company driving the next objective now that the supply has caught up. The deep gamble paid.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT THRUST
forks.trigger: The spearhead culminated short, or the reinforcements caught it exhausted at the objective; the axis stalled in enemy depth.
forks.consequence: The thrust has stalled with empty racks deep in {TARGET_FACTION}'s interior, the reserves closing and the flanks exposed. The next operation is to extract the spearhead before it is cut off and destroyed — a fighting withdrawal back toward the railhead, trading the ground won to save the company. The offensive overreached; the bill comes due.

storyElementSeed: A crew chief reading a fuel gauge by torchlight at a halt deep in enemy country, doing the sum twice, then telling the commander the number flat and waiting to hear whether they go on or stop.

is-kurita.objectives.primary: Seize the junction and hold it before the spearhead spends its last, cutting the enemy's lateral movement and making the Dragon's breakthrough permanent. The deepest thrust is the one that must not stop short of the goal.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Take the road junction and its supply stocks and hold the position before the advance outruns its own ledger; an offensive that culminates short has spent its capital for nothing, so secure the forward depot that funds the next bound.

inspiration: Rather than assault a heavily fortified strongpoint, the campaign bypasses it and seizes the lightly held waystation system behind it, cutting the fortress off to wither while the advance moves on.
skeleton: the player's company seizes a lightly held logistics waystation that sits behind a powerful bypassed fortress, cutting the fortress off to wither rather than storming it, where the prize is the connector not the strongpoint, the defender of the waystation is light but its loss strands a far heavier force, and speed beats the fortress's reaction
title: OPERATION LEAPFROG
situation: {TARGET_FACTION} has poured its strength into the fortress at the front of {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}, and {EMPLOYER} has decided not to oblige it. The fortress is strong, dug in, and ready for the assault everyone expects — so the assault will not come. Instead the campaign goes around it. Your company takes the prize that makes the fortress irrelevant: the logistics waystation behind it, the depot and transit node that feeds the strongpoint and links it to the rest of the defense. Take the waystation and the fortress becomes an island — strong, intact, and cut off, left to starve on its own stores while the advance moves past it. {NPC:intel-source} reads the waystation as lightly held: a security company at most, Regular quality, guarding a depot that was never meant to be the front line, because the fortress was supposed to keep the front line far away. That picture is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and a depot's garrison can be reinforced if the defender guesses the plan. The open ground is the whole opportunity. The waystation sits in the fortress's rear, on the open transit ground the strongpoint exists to protect. So reaching it is a race against the fortress's reaction, not a fight through its guns. Get to the waystation fast, take it before the fortress can detach a force to save it, and hold it long enough to make the cut permanent. The prize is the connector, not the strongpoint. A company drawn into fighting the fortress has lost the point of the mission, which is to leave the fortress alone and take the depot behind it. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the sector and, once he sees the move, will try to pull weight back from the fortress to relieve the waystation. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Take the waystation and strand the fortress, or get tangled with the strongpoint and let the connector stay open.

objectives.primary: Seize the logistics waystation behind the bypassed fortress and hold it long enough to cut the strongpoint's supply and communications, stranding the fortress while the advance moves on.
objectives.secondary: Capture the waystation's transit records and depot stocks intact. The records map the defender's whole logistics network, and the stocks turn the captured node into a usable forward base.
objectives.bonus: Destroy or capture the fortress's relief column if it sorties to save the waystation. A fortress that spends its mobile reserve trying to keep the connector is weaker still once it is finally stranded.

complications.name: Leave the Fortress Alone
complications.text: The fortress is a magnet and a trap. It is right there, strong and obvious, and every instinct says a force in its rear should deal with it. But the plan is to ignore it — to take the waystation and let the strongpoint starve — and a company that gets drawn into trading fire with the fortress has abandoned the operation for the fight the defender would much rather have.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Engaging the fortress directly draws its full prepared strength and pulls the company off the time-critical waystation seizure. The objective is the waystation.
